nodes.summary: Let $P(x, y) = 6(x - y/2)(x - y/2 - 3/2) + x + y + 2$. For $m = 7$ and $n = 12$ (the sector of slope $12/7$), the step difference of $P$ is $k = 3$: with $l = \gcd(6, 12) = 6$, one has $P(1, 2) - P(0, 0) = 3$.
nodes.title: Step difference of the slope-$12/7$ example

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m, n$ and a real function $P(x, y)$ of two real variables, let $l = \gcd(m \mathbin{\dot-} 1, n)$, where $m \mathbin{\dot-} 1$ is subtraction truncated at $0$ (so $l = n$ when $m = 0$). The step difference of $P$ for the sector of slope $n/m$ is $k = P((m - 1)/l, n/l) - P(0, 0)$, with $m - 1$ here the real difference and division by $l = 0$ read as $0$: the change…
nodes.title: Step difference

nodes.summary: If $P$ is a quadratic packing polynomial on a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, then for every point $(x, y) \in S$ the value $P(x, y)$ is a natural number.
nodes.title: Quadratic packing polynomials take natural-number values

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be coprime positive integers, let $l = \gcd(m - 1, n)$, and assume that $n/l$ divides $l$. Let $k$ be a positive integer with $k \equiv (m - 1)/l \pmod{n/l}$, let $F$ be a real number, and let $\hat P(x, y) = \frac{n}{2} x \left(x - \frac{k}{n/l}\right) + x + \frac{k}{n/l} y + F$. Let $M(x, y) = (x - \frac{m - 1}{n} y, y)$ and let $\hat I(n/m) = M(I(n/m))$ be the image under $M$ of the lattice points…
nodes.title: Sheared criterion for quadratic packing polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $M(x, y) = (x - y/2, y)$ and let $\hat I(12/7) = M(I(12/7))$ be the image under $M$ of the lattice points $I(12/7)$ of the sector of slope $12/7$. Then $\hat P(x, y) = 6x(x - 3/2) + x + \frac{3}{2} y + 2$ is a quadratic packing polynomial on $\hat I(12/7)$.
nodes.title: The slope-$12/7$ example on the sheared sector

nodes.summary: A real function $P(x, y)$ of two real variables is a quadratic packing polynomial (QPP) on a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ if it is a polynomial of total degree two, that is, $P(x, y) = a x^2 + b x y + c y^2 + d x + e y + f$ for some real $a, b, c, d, e, f$ with $a, b, c$ not all zero, and $P$ maps $S$ bijectively onto the set $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ of natural numbers.
nodes.title: Quadratic packing polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be coprime positive integers, let $l = \gcd(m - 1, n)$, and let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice points $I(n/m)$ of the sector of slope $n/m$. If the step difference of $P$ for $m, n$ is a positive integer $k$, then $P(0, 0) = \frac{l^2}{n} (k - 1)(k + 1)/12$.
nodes.title: Constant term of a quadratic packing polynomial on a rational sector

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be coprime positive integers, let $l = \gcd(m - 1, n)$, and let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice points $I(n/m)$ of the sector of slope $n/m$ whose step difference for $m, n$ is a positive integer $k$. Put $F = P(0, 0)$ and $\hat P(x, y) = P(x + \frac{m - 1}{n} y, y)$, and let $\bar y_k$ be the height of the first step of the $k$-th staircase of the sector. Then…
nodes.title: First step value and sheared form of a quadratic packing polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be coprime positive integers, let $l = \gcd(m - 1, n)$, and let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice points $I(n/m)$ of the sector of slope $n/m$ whose step difference for $m, n$ is a positive integer $k$. nodes.title: Step-difference form of a quadratic packing polynomial on a rational sector

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be coprime positive integers and let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice points $I(n/m)$ of the sector of slope $n/m$. Then $n$ divides $(m - 1)^2$, and there are integers $D, E, F$ such that for all real $x, y$
nodes.title: Stanton's form of a quadratic packing polynomial on a rational sector

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha > 0$ be a real number and let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice sector $I(\alpha)$. Then there are integers $A, B, C, D, E, F$ with $A > 0$, $B^2 = AC$ and $\alpha = A/(1 - B)$ such that for all real $x, y$
nodes.title: Form of a quadratic packing polynomial on a sector (Gjaldbæk)

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be positive coprime integers, let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice sector $I(n/m)$, and suppose that the step difference of $P$ equals a positive integer $k$. Then for every natural number $i$, every point $p$ of the staircase $J_i$ and every point $q$ of the staircase $J_{i+k}$, the difference $P(q) - P(p)$ is an integer multiple of $k$.
nodes.title: Staircase congruence for quadratic packing polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be positive coprime integers and $l = \gcd(m - 1, n)$, let $P$ be a quadratic packing polynomial on the lattice sector $I(n/m)$, and suppose that the step difference of $P$ equals a positive integer $k$. Then the first height of the staircase $J_k$ is $\bar y_k = n/l - 1$.
nodes.title: Height of the first step of the k-th staircase

nodes.summary: For a real number $\alpha$, let $S(\alpha) = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 0 \le y \le \alpha x\}$ be the sector of slope $\alpha$. Its lattice points are $I(\alpha) = S(\alpha) \cap \mathbb{Z}^2$, viewed as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Lattice points of a sector

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m, n, i$, let $l = \gcd(m - 1, n)$. The $i$-th staircase of the sector of slope $n/m$ is $J_i = \{(x, y) \in I(n/m) : nx - (m - 1)y = li\}$, where $I(n/m)$ is the set of lattice points of that sector.
nodes.title: Staircases of a rational sector

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m, n$, the first height of the staircase $J_0$ of the sector of slope $n/m$ is $\bar y_0 = 0$; indeed the origin lies on $J_0$.
nodes.title: The zeroth staircase starts at height zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m, n, i$, the first height $\bar y_i$ of the staircase $J_i$ of the sector of slope $n/m$ is the least $y$-coordinate of a point of $J_i$, that is, the height of its first step; it is $0$ if $J_i$ is empty.
nodes.title: First height of a staircase

nodes.summary: For every real number $\alpha$, the origin $(0, 0)$ lies in the set $I(\alpha)$ of lattice points of the sector of slope $\alpha$.
nodes.title: The origin is a lattice point of every sector

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m, n$, the origin $(0, 0)$ lies on the staircase $J_0$ of the sector of slope $n/m$.
nodes.title: The origin lies on the zeroth staircase

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
